title: Steve Eisman Reveals His Personal Portfolio: Every Position Explained
summary: Eisman explains his concentrated long portfolio through AI suppliers, electricity infrastructure, low-valued turnarounds, established franchises and speculative cannabis. He sells capital-intensive platforms while monitoring AI financing and power bottlenecks. NVIDIA growth and the infrastructure backlog support current demand, but most valuation and recovery theses remain undated or conditional. Charter and Meritage still face operating pressure. Apple already had its own models, Microsoft had raised debt since its IPO, and Progressive did not invent direct insurance. Glass House upside rests on unproven market access, prices and margins; scenario arithmetic is separated from investable outcomes.
assessment: A useful statement of holdings, catalysts and falsifiers, with several factual errors in supporting premises. The central multi-year and conditional investment theses should not be graded as completed returns. Capital-intensity rotation has evidence, while stock-specific valuation claims lack point-in-time consensus reconstruction. Cannabis rescheduling is real but narrower than an automatic opening of every market.
speaker_map_notes: SPEAKER_00 is Steve Eisman throughout this solo portfolio discussion, established by first-person holdings and self-identification.
framework_points: Write the initial thesis and sell when it fails rather than rationalizing thesis creep.
Distinguish growth stories from fundamentals and recognize uncertainty at regime changes.
Separate AI suppliers from buyers bearing the capital-spending burden.
Use cash flow, buybacks, book value, ROE and backlog to identify catalysts.
Model speculative outcomes with explicit margins and dilution rather than a single target.
State concrete evidence that would reduce portfolio risk.
tools_and_charts: Sixteen-position portfolio grouped into five themes
AIG ROE and tangible book value
Glass House price-volume-margin and enterprise-value scenarios
transcript_cautions: All captions identify one speaker. Company spelling and tickers are normalized only where context is clear: Novo Nordisk, Meritage/MTH and Taylor Morrison/TMHC.
Publication is July 1 but references to an upcoming NYSE listing likely reflect earlier recording; Glass House began NYSE trading June 30.
Position counts are not portfolio market-value weights.
Several forward EPS multiples and growth figures lack stated price dates or GAAP/adjusted conventions.
The Glass House valuation chart is discussed but its complete debt and share-count inputs are absent from the transcript.
The brief sentence near 1419-1429 seconds is incomplete, so no missing comparison is reconstructed.
